For every complete real inner-product space E (with its normed additive commutative group structure), every f:E→ℝ, and all real α, β, h, assume f is continuously Fréchet differentiable on all of E and α-strongly convex on all of E: for every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1],
f((1-t)x+t y)≤(1-t)f(x)+t f(y)-(α/2)t(1-t)‖y-x‖².
Assume also α>0, h>0, βh≤1, αh≤1, and the global quadratic upper inequality for every x,y∈E,
f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y-x⟩+(β/2)‖y-x‖²,
where ∇f is the Riesz gradient. Then for every initial point x₀∈E, every comparator z∈E, and every natural number N>0, let xₖ₊₁=xₖ-h∇f(xₖ) with the same fixed step throughout, and set q=1-αh. Both following conclusions hold with the indicated scope:
(1) f(x_N)-f(z)≤α q^N ‖x₀-z‖²/[2(1-q^N)].
(2) If αh<1, then f(x_N)-f(z)≤[α/(2(q^(-N)-1))]‖x₀-z‖².
The first conclusion is unconditional under the common hypotheses. Only the second is conditional on αh<1. Here q^N is a natural-number power and q^(-N) is a negative integer power, equal to the inverse of q^N. The common hypotheses imply 0≤q<1. Thus 1-q^N>0 for N>0. At the permitted endpoint αh=1, q=0 and the first bound is f(x_N)-f(z)≤0; the second implication supplies no bound at this endpoint. Under its strict hypothesis 0<q<1, the second denominator is positive and the two displayed right sides agree. Lean's inverse is totalized at zero, but this does not extend the conditional second conclusion to q=0. N=0, α=0, and h=0 are excluded. If x₀=z, the right side of the first bound is zero, as is that of the second whenever its condition holds. No explicit sign assumption on β is present. No finite-dimensionality, optimizer or stationary-point condition on z, existence of a minimizer, or gradient Lipschitz assumption is stated. The quantified comparator z is arbitrary in E. These are last-iterate function-value inequalities, with no additional distance-contraction or limit claim.
